references.text: Moses asks to find favor in God's eyes and that God should go with the people, the same theme of grace and God's presence
Moses prays again that the Lord should go among the people, a direct follow-up to the prayer in Exod 33:16
Israel is set apart from other peoples because God is near them, the same idea of being separated from all nations on earth
Israel is described as a people who live by themselves and do not count themselves among the nations, parallel to the thought of being set apart
Israel shall be God's own possession, chosen among all peoples, the same theme of being separated from all nations
David praises that Israel is unique among all peoples on earth; God has made them his people
Christ gave himself to cleanse a people who are his own, set apart from others, fulfilling the idea of a separate people
Believers are a chosen race, a people belonging to God, separated from other nations
Clear theological contrast: God sets apart Israel for grace (Exodus), while he destroys enemies from the nations in judgment (Ezekiel).
Contrast between Cain's fear of being without God's face (a fugitive) and Moses' prayer that God's presence should define Israel's identity.
Theological contrast: Jeremiah warns that grace is withdrawn and the people are exiled, while Exodus emphasizes that God's presence is what keeps grace and identity intact.
